surname_desc: Moon (文) is Korea's 23rd most common surname at about 0.9%. The character means 'literature, writing' — fittingly, the Nampyeong Moon clan produced many distinguished scholars.

short: Someone refined, with eloquence
meaning: 아론 (雅論, Aron) joins 아 (雅, a), "elegant and refined," with 론 (論, ron), "discourse, wisdom." It matches "Aaron," the biblical first high priest — globally resonant. K-pop fans may recall Aron of NU'EST. It's a boy's name, refined and international — a polished impression.
surname_desc: Kim (金) is Korea's most common surname, held by about 21.5% of the population — roughly one in five Koreans. The major lineages, the Gimhae and Gyeongju Kim clans, trace back to Silla royalty.

short: A white and shining person
meaning: 백호 (白晧, Baekho) joins 백 (白, baek), "pure white," with 호 (晧, ho), "bright and luminous." Above all, 백호 (白虎) is the "White Tiger," the guardian of the west among the Four Symbols — a brave, sacred image. Firm and spirited, familiar too from Slam Dunk's Kang Baek-ho — a bold, dashing impression.
surname_desc: Jin (陳) is around Korea's 48th most common surname at about 0.3%. The Yeoyang Jin clan traces to a Song Chinese official who settled in Goryeo; the sound is crisp and memorable.

short: All good things come in native Korean
meaning: 다온 (Da-on) is a native Korean name — the native Korean word for "all good things come." It carries no Chinese characters; the meaning lives right in the sound. Balanced in sound, one syllable open and one closed
surname_desc: Park (朴) is Korea's third most common surname at about 8.4%. Uniquely native to Korea, it descends from Bak Hyeokgeose, the legendary founding king of the Silla Kingdom.

short: Someone wise who holds a steady center
meaning: 예중 (叡中, Yejung) pairs 예 (叡, ye), "bright and wise," with 중 (中, jung), "center, balanced." It pictures someone wise who holds a steady center. Neat and balanced, it also reads like a short form of "arts middle school," hinting at artistry. Wisdom and steadiness meet in an upright, settled name.

short: Someone broad-minded who stands tall
meaning: 범준 (汎峻, Beomjun) joins 범 (汎, beom), "broad, far-reaching," with 준 (峻, jun), "lofty and towering." It's a boy's name meaning someone broad-minded who stands tall. 범 lends a magnanimous vessel; 준 is among the most beloved, as in 민준 (Minjun) — a confident, trendy impression.
surname_desc: Lee (李) is Korea's second most common surname at about 14.7% of the population. Its most famous lineage, the Jeonju Lee clan, founded the Joseon Dynasty and ruled Korea for over 500 years.

short: Someone clean as water and bright as the dawn
meaning: 근우 (漌旭, Geunu) joins 근 (漌, geun), "clear water," with 우 (旭, u), "the rising sun." It pictures someone clean as water and bright as the dawn. Soft and stylish, its 우 ending is one of the most loved today — 준우 (Junu), 지우 (Jiu). Clarity and brightness together give it a trendy yet easy feel.
surname_desc: Seo (徐) is Korea's 13th most common surname at about 1.5%. The Dalseong and Icheon Seo clans produced distinguished scholars, including famed Joseon-era prime ministers.

short: Someone warm who stands tall like a mountain
meaning: 남준 (南峻, Namjun) joins 남 (南, nam), "south, warmth," with 준 (峻, jun), "lofty and towering." It pictures someone warm who stands tall like a mountain. Clear and firm, its 준 ending is the most loved in boys' names. Above all, K-pop fans will instantly think of BTS's leader RM (Kim Nam-joon) — an intelligent, leaderly name.
surname_desc: Lee (李) is Korea's second most common surname at about 14.7% of the population. Its most famous lineage, the Jeonju Lee clan, founded the Joseon Dynasty and ruled Korea for over 500 years.

short: Someone who shines like a star, bright as noon
meaning: 루오 (婁旿, Ruo) joins 루 (婁, ru), "a star," with 오 (旿, o), "bright, the midday sun." It's a boy's name meaning someone who shines like a star, bright as noon. Short and distinctive with no final consonants, it sounds exotic abroad — an uncommon yet bright impression.
